This tetra is the most gracile of the so-called "rosy tetras". The rosy tetras are a species-rich clade of tetras that share the following characters: a comparatively deep body, a humeral spot (the spot on the shoulder), long fins in males and, in females, an obvious white-black-white marking in the dorsal fin. The phantom tetras, rosy tetras, bleeding hearts and so on belong to that group.

Fully grown specimens are about 4 cm long.

Hyphessobrycon copelandi is a sought-after species. This can be concluded from the fact that it has a quite well-known common name in German: Federsalmler, which means "Feather tetra". Nevertheless it is extremely rare in the trade. Most often, enthusiasts had to pick up single specimens out of importations of cardinal tetras.

A good number of fully grown specimens (about 4 cm long) have now been imported from Brazil, so perhaps a breeder will now build up an aquarium population of this pretty fish.
